1.

Short counter affdidavit along with Vakalatnama filed by Ms. Amrita Singh, Advocate on behalf of
opposite party no.2/ informant are taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2/ informant,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused material brought on record.

3. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred for quashing of the charge sheet dated 13.04.2018 as well as entire proceedings, including cognizance/summoning order dated 03.07.2018, of Case No.4456 of 2018 (State Vs. Wajid Ali and others), arising out of Case Crime No.0124 of 2017, under Sections 498A, 323 IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Bareilly, pending before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bareilly.

sentences.text: 1 4. It has been submitted by learned counsel for applicant that applicant is husband of opposite party no.2 and there had been some matrimonial dispute between them.
The marriage of applicant with opposite party no.2 has taken place in the year 2013 and out of that marriage they have three children.
During pendency of the case, both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter.
Both the parties have filed an application for compromise before the trial Court but the offences are non compoundable.
Both the parties are living together and now the informant does not want to pursue the impugned proceedings.

Referring to these facts, it was stated that in view of these facts and circumstances, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the impugned proceedings pending and thus, the impugned proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

5. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2/informant has concurred with the arguments of learned counsel for the applicant and submitted that both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter and now they are residing together.
The informant does not want to proceed with the case pending before the trial court and the impugned proceedings may be quashed, as no useful purpose would be served by exhausting remedy of trial.
6. Learned A.G.A. has no objection if parties compromise the matter.
7. I have considered the submissions and perused the record.
8. It is well settled that in appropriate cases, criminal proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise between the parties.
In the instant case, applicant is husband of opposite party no.2 and there had been some matrimonial dispute between them.
The marriage of applicant with opposite party no.2 has taken place way back in the year 2013 and out of that marriage they have three children.
It was submitted on behalf of both the parties that both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter and now they are residing together happily.
The informant does not want to proceed with the case against the applicant.
Both the parties have already compromise before the trial Court.
Counter affidavit of informant is on record.

Considering the law laid down in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296 and the facts of the matter, it would be in the interest of justice that the impugned proceedings be quashed, as the continuance of the same would be nothing but wastage of time of Court.

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In view of the aforesaid, the impugned entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case including charge-sheet and summoning order, against applicant, namely, Wajid Ali, are hereby, quashed.
10. The application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed.
